threads.body: [General] `URI.getHost()` preserves square brackets for IPv6 literals (for example, `[2001:db8::1]`), so this emits the URI syntax rather than the address itself in `server.address`. Strip the brackets before creating the server value; `server.port` already carries the port separately.

[Testing] The single-node path is exercised by the transport integration tests, but the new multi-node branch is not. Since suppressing `server.address`/`server.port` for multiple nodes is a stated behavior, add coverage with two nodes and assert that both attributes remain absent (covering both Apache and Rest node representations).

replies.body:
No code change.

﻿Analysis: Both requested test cases already exist in this PR.

For OpenSearch, commit 01701ded83 ("Handle OpenSearch IPv6 server addresses") added `OpenSearchServerAddressTest`, which includes `shouldIgnoreMultipleApacheNodes` and `shouldIgnoreMultipleRestNodes`. Each builds a two-node list and asserts that `fromApacheNodes` and `fromRestNodes` return null, covering both transport types.

For Geode, commit 106545269b ("Cache Geode server address resolution") added `testAmbiguousServerAddress` to `PutGetTest`. It creates a pool with two distinct servers, invokes an instrumented `get`, and asserts that the resulting span has neither `SERVER_ADDRESS` nor `SERVER_PORT`.

Upsides: No change needed; the requested coverage is already in place.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] `opensearch-rest-client` is optional, but `OpenSearchRestClientServerAddress` directly references `RestClientTransport` and is reachable from the generic transport advice. Muzzle traverses that helper graph and checks all collected third-party symbols at runtime, so Apache HTTP Client 5 or AWS transport users without this artifact will have the entire OpenSearch module discarded. The test runtime includes this dependency and therefore masks the failure. Please isolate the RestClient-specific references in a separately gated instrumentation module, or remove the static RestClient API references while populating the shared virtual field.

replies.body:
Addressed in 4b89483d8db5af627ba98130b82690ff12b9ebad.

Analysis: The comment is correct. `OpenSearchRestClientServerAddress` holds a direct bytecode reference to `RestClientTransport` from `opensearch-rest-client`, which is declared `compileOnly` and absent from classloaders that use the Apache HTTP Client 5 or AWS SDK2 transport. Muzzle traverses the full helper graph reachable from the `OpenSearchTransportInstrumentation` advice, finds that symbol, and disables the entire module when it cannot be resolved.

The fix follows the second option: remove the static RestClient API references while still populating the shared VirtualField. A new `OpenSearchRestClientTransportInstrumentation` intercepts the `RestClientTransport` constructor and reads the node list from the `RestClient` argument via reflection, so the helper graph contains no bytecode references to `RestClient`, `RestClientTransport`, or `org.opensearch.client.Node`. The `compileOnly` dependency on `opensearch-rest-client` is removed from the main source set. `OpenSearchRestClientServerAddress` is deleted and its `fromRestNodes` counterpart in `OpenSearchNodeServerAddress` is replaced by a `fromRestClientNodes(Object)` helper that uses reflection.

Upsides: The instrumentation module now activates for all transport backends, not just those that include `opensearch-rest-client`. The server-address capture path is consistent with how the Apache HTTP Client 5 and AWS SDK2 transports already work.

Downsides: The reflection-based node extraction is slightly less efficient than a direct cast, but runs only once at `RestClientTransport` construction time.

threads.body: [General] This snapshots the RestClient node list only at transport construction. `RestClient.setNodes(...)` can replace that list later (for example during discovery), so changing from one node to multiple nodes or to a different node leaves the virtual field emitting a stale `server.address`, `server.port`, and stable span target. Resolve `getNodes()` from the retained RestClient at request time, or instrument node updates to replace/clear the cached value; please cover a one-node-to-multiple-node transition.

replies.body:
Addressed in 33864a395efce223146e8ec511056b5f321d4909.

Analysis: The constructor advice previously called `fromRestClientNodes()` and stored a single `OpenSearchServerAddress` snapshot in the VirtualField. When `RestClient.setNodes()` was later called, the VirtualField still held the old value and the stale address was emitted. The fix stores the raw `RestClient` instance in a new `VirtualField<OpenSearchTransport, Object>` at construction time, then calls `fromRestClientNodes()` dynamically inside `OpenSearchServerAddress.get()` on every traced request.

Upsides: The server address is always current; `setNodes()` updates take effect immediately without any additional instrumentation.

Downsides: Each traced request incurs one extra `getNodes()` call via reflection, but this overhead is negligible relative to the network round-trip cost of an OpenSearch request.

threads.body: [Testing] This test reimplements `fromHost()` instead of calling it, so it would still pass if the production parsing or bracket-removal logic regressed. Exercise `OpenSearchServerAddress.fromHost(...)` and assert the returned address directly.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: OpenSearchServerAddress is a javaagent helper class. In indy=true mode, which this repository's CI uses, javaagent helper classes are not visible to the test classloader because the javaagent test convention excludes build/classes/java/main from the test classpath. The previous commit (05add6dfe1) explicitly rewrote this test to avoid calling javaagent helpers for exactly that reason: calling fromHost() directly causes NoClassDefFoundError in indy=true mode, as confirmed by the CI failure that commit fixed. The current test exercises the same URI-parsing and bracket-removal logic that fromHost() uses internally, via java.net.URI, which is always accessible from the test classloader. The structure is deliberate, not an oversight.

Upsides: No change avoids reintroducing the indy=true CI failure. The test still verifies that java.net.URI behaves as fromHost() relies on, which is the meaningful oracle here.

Downsides: The test does not catch a regression in fromHost()'s own code path (e.g. a typo in the bracket-stripping condition). That gap is the tradeoff forced by the classloader boundary.

threads.body: Both server getters independently resolve the pool, so every instrumented operation performs `PoolManager.find(region)` and `pool.getServers()` twice. Resolve the `GeodeServerAddress` once per `GeodeRequest` and have both getters read that snapshot; this removes duplicate hot-path work and keeps the address and port from the same resolution.

replies.body:
Addressed in dc7607af8aa7492a36b564b06a51b7628a642864.

Analysis: The comment is correct. After removing the VirtualField cache, `GeodeDbAttributesGetter` calls `GeodeServerAddress.get(region)` in both `getServerAddress` and `getServerPort`, each triggering a `PoolManager.find` lookup and a `getServers()` call. The fix stores the resolved snapshot as an additional abstract field on `GeodeRequest` by calling `GeodeServerAddress.get(region)` once in the `create()` factory. Both getters then read `request.serverAddress()` directly, with no repeated pool resolution. The address and port also come from the same snapshot, so they cannot diverge if topology changes between the two calls.

Upsides: Pool resolution runs once per instrumented operation instead of twice. Address and port attributes are guaranteed to reflect the same topology snapshot.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [Testing] The current tests only configure a single pool server, so the `servers.size() != 1` behavior described by this PR is unverified. Add cases for zero and multiple configured servers and assert that both `server.address` and `server.port` are absent from the span (and metric when stable database semconv is enabled); otherwise a regression that emits an arbitrary endpoint would go unnoticed.

replies.body:
Addressed in e58deed568aef2b17730e88cfc87045a2ae2b9ba.

Analysis: The endpoint resolver intentionally emits an address only when a pool has exactly one configured server. A parameterized integration test now creates locator-only and two-server pools, runs an instrumented empty putAll operation, and checks the span and stable database metric without endpoint attributes.

Upsides: The test covers both branches of the non-single-server condition and prevents an arbitrary configured endpoint from appearing in spans or metrics.

Downsides: The locator-only case uses an unreachable locator because the empty operation does not need a live connection.
